references.text: The priest shall examine the wound and see if the hair has turned white, which is a sign of leprosy
Describes white spots on the skin that must be examined by the priest
Raw flesh (living flesh) in the wound is a sign of uncleanness, the same sign mentioned in verse 10
White hair and white spots that go deeper than the skin are signs of leprosy
The priest shall examine the swelling and declare the person unclean if there is leprosy
Summary of the laws concerning swellings, rashes, and spots to determine cleanliness or uncleanness
Reminder to follow the priests' guidance regarding leprosy
